I need to decide on an auction bid for Marvin Gardens.

I have $889 and the dark blue monopoly. The auction is at $76 with a minimum bid of $77. I previously considered walking away for roughly $160 to $180.

I should not set a ceiling. p1 has $320 and developed oranges, so I must watch for a cash drain. Dark blues will stay unbuilt until my cushion is safe. Ventnor from p4 is the real priority; he only has $29.

p4 now owns the green monopoly (North Carolina and Pennsylvania). He also has brown hotels, light blues, three railroads, Ventnor, and Water Works. He is nearly broke with only $29 cash.

p2 has a dangerous pink monopoly with houses and $74 cash. p1 has an orange monopoly with houses and is in jail with $320. Building the dark blue houses costs $400 total.

I am calculating exact rent values to judge the threat level. New York Avenue with three houses pays $650, Tennessee with two pays $200, and Virginia with three pays $500. I still need to verify States Avenue at three houses.

States Avenue at three houses pays $450. Virginia and New York are $500 and $650. I can survive one of those hits with my $889.

Marvin Gardens is listed at $280 but mortgaged for $140. p2 called anything under $140 free money because the mortgage value is $140. I already own Atlantic Avenue. Ventnor from p4 is still needed to complete the yellow set.

I will bid incrementally rather than jump to my ceiling. A small raise to $77 keeps p1 in the auction and drains his cash. If he continues matching, I can raise to roughly $160–$180 before dropping out.

p1 just bid $76 after I bid $75. They are nickel-and-diming. I will keep the incremental war going. Each dollar drains p1 before he gets out of jail. He might need cash when he leaves. If I let him win cheaply, he gets a $280 property and blocks my yellow path. I can hold two yellows now and trade for Ventnor later if p4 busts.

Mortgaging the property back would only return $140, so paying $77 and mortgaging is not a net gain. The real value is the two-thirds yellow position and blocking others. I must weigh p1’s reduced cash cushion against my own need for funds to build dark blues and survive rent hits.

I calculated the exact cash impact of buying Marvin at $150. That would leave me with $739, which is too low to survive a New York rent of $650 after building one house on Boardwalk. Even two houses would leave only $339, making survival impossible. My current $889 cushion can cover both a New York and a Virginia hit.

Building one house on Boardwalk leaves $689, which barely survives a New York rent of $650. Two houses leave $489, which cannot cover Virginia at $500 but can survive a Baltic hotel at $450. The orange threat is the binding constraint. I am now recalculating the walk-away price because the earlier estimate of $160–$180 seems too high.

The absolute survival ceiling is $239. That leaves exactly zero cash after a New York rent of $650. Dark blue houses are the only way to win, because unbuilt properties pay very little rent. Park Place with a monopoly pays $70 and Boardwalk pays $100.

Dark blue house values are severe. One house yields $175 on Park Place and $200 on Boardwalk. Two houses pay $500 and $600. The real win is building dark blues, not chasing a yellow set that needs Ventnor from p4, who already owns a green monopoly and brown hotels. Still, paying under $100 for Marvin is smart because it blocks p1 from snapping up a cheap asset.

If p1 wins at $76, they can mortgage the property for $140 and profit $64 cash. That would leave them with roughly $384. I must decide how high to push the bid to block this steal. p2 already told p1 that anything under $140 is free money, so p1 may raise toward that level.

The mortgage arbitrage is not viable. Unmortgaging would cost $154, so the net gain is only $63 and the property would be lost. I will not pursue this path. I will bid incrementally to stay in the auction and drain p1's cash.

I am reassessing the true value of Marvin Gardens. It does not complete the yellow monopoly, so its worth is tied to the future acquisition of Ventnor from p4. p4 currently owns North Carolina and has a green monopoly, brown hotels, and three railroads, making him property-rich but cash-poor. The two-thirds yellow set would be powerful once Ventnor is added, since houses on those properties cost $150 each.

Marvin Gardens is worth only $24 in rent by itself. No other player can complete the yellow monopoly; p4 already holds Ventnor, and p1 and p2 have no yellows. Only I can finish that set, so the property is a single asset for everyone else. Denying it to p1 is mainly about blocking a cheap acquisition rather than completing a path.

Marvin is uniquely valuable to me as the missing link to the yellow monopoly. I should bid higher than the other players, but not so high that it prevents building dark blues or surviving rent hits. Ventnor is listed at $260, and p4 may be willing to sell it if desperate.

I am now targeting a bid of $120 to $140. This sits below my earlier $160–$180 ceiling and respects the $140 mortgage floor. I will raise incrementally, perhaps to $77 or $80–90, to show resolve without descending into a dollar-by-dollar war that wastes cash.

I will bid $77 and keep my public message calm. I am weighing whether to jump to $140 to knock p1 out, since they may be chasing the $140 mortgage arbitrage p2 advertised.

The mortgage arbitrage is now the deciding factor. If p1 bids $139, they can mortgage the property for $140 and profit $61. To stop them, I must bid $140 or higher. At that price, I would pay $140 for a property worth $280, netting zero cash and leaving it mortgaged. The only value above the mortgage floor is the strategic path to the yellow monopoly. I am weighing whether that path justifies paying $140.

The yellow monopoly would cost $450 to $1,350 to build, and its three-house rent would be $800 to $850. Dark blue is already complete, so buying a speculative yellow piece is a poor use of cash right now. At $140, I would still have $749 left, but that is not enough to build a second house on Boardwalk and survive a New York rent of $650.

Building one house on Boardwalk after buying Marvin at $140 leaves only $349, which cannot survive a New York rent of $650. Without the purchase, $749 still covers that hit with $99 left over. The dark blue monopoly pays double rent while unbuilt, but houses are the real win condition. The priority is surviving orange and pink rent hits first, then building dark blue houses when safe.

A $77 bid leaves $812 cash, which is too little to build a house and survive a New York rent of $650. The only way to do both is to spend under $39 on Marvin, which is impossible. I am on CHANCE, so I do not need to build now. I will wait until after the auction to decide whether to build.

The binding constraint for this auction is bankruptcy risk, not the yellow monopoly. The worst rent hits are New York at three houses ($650), Virginia at three houses ($500), and States at three houses ($450). With $889 cash, I can afford a New York hit and still have $239 left over. That means my maximum bid is $239, or $189 if I want a $50 cushion. I will not spend more than that.

The $76 bid is safely below my $160–$180 walk-away price, so I will raise to $77 and keep the public message neutral. I am watching for p1 to try to push me higher, but small increments protect me from overpaying. I will not confirm that I will bid $140, because p2’s earlier comment about the $140 mortgage arbitrage may be encouraging p1 to keep raising. I am prioritizing winning the auction over minimizing decision rounds.

p1 is in jail with $320, so draining their cash would hurt them more than me. I will not chase past my walk-away price to punish them; if p1 overpays, letting them have the property still wastes their money. I will bid $77 and keep the public message strategic.

I will not pressure p1 with a message about their jail status or the mortgage arbitrage. That could encourage them to keep raising. I will simply bid $77 and stay silent.
